question_text: Why is Mendel considered as the father of Genetics?

The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: His experiments
steps.why: The title rests on what he did: controlled crosses (hybridization) between pea plants with contrasting characters gave him the counts his laws came from.
common_mistakes: Writing 'pea plants' without 'hybridization experiments' — the experiment type is the marked phrase.
Naming fruit flies — those were Morgan's material, not Mendel's.
steps.memory_tip: Picture Mendel in a garden of pea plants — peas are the one material tied to his name.
steps.margin_note: One line on the experiments, one step on the laws.

steps.label: His laws

lines.text: He introduced the laws of inheritance.

steps.why: The reason he is 'father of Genetics' is the conclusion he drew: the laws of inheritance, the founding laws of the whole subject.
common_mistakes: Writing 'law of evolution' — evolution goes with Darwin; inheritance goes with Mendel.
Trying to list the laws by name and mixing them up — the phrase 'laws of inheritance' is enough here.
steps.memory_tip: Genetics is the study of inheritance; its father is the man who wrote inheritance's first laws.
steps.margin_note: The boxed law line plus the because-sentence completes the answer.

insider_note: Two marked phrases decide this answer: 'hybridization experiments on pea plants' and 'laws of inheritance' — write both exactly.
